Irrawadi, also known as Irrawadi Devi, is the revered Pearl Serpent Goddess in Southeast Asian mythology. She is often depicted as a magnificent serpent with glistening scales, adorned with precious pearls that symbolize her divine power and wisdom.

According to legend, Irrawadi is the guardian of the rivers and waterways, including the mighty Irrawaddy River in Myanmar. She is believed to bring fertility and abundance to the lands along her river, and her blessings are sought by farmers, fishermen, and those who rely on the river for their livelihood.

As the Pearl Serpent Goddess, Irrawadi is associated with prosperity, fertility, and protection. She is also revered as a symbol of transformation and regeneration, as the river she guards is known for its changing currents and ever-shifting landscape. Many myths and stories are told about her wondrous deeds, from granting wishes to protecting her devotees from harm.

Irrawadi is often portrayed as a benevolent and majestic deity, respected and honored by the local communities along the Irrawaddy River and beyond. She is celebrated in various festivals and rituals, where offerings are made to her to seek her favor and blessings. Her divine presence is felt by many as a source of strength, guidance, and protection, as she watches over the precious waters of the Irrawaddy River and its surrounding lands.
